# VP9 sub-64 dimensions: classification and backend decision

**AI disclosure:** this document was generated by AI at the contributor's request.

Research record for [omarchy-m1-video#12](https://github.com/iconidentify/omarchy-m1-video/issues/12).
It decides the supported boundary for VP9 streams whose coded frame is narrower or
shorter than 64 pixels. It does **not** claim that any of the 60 affected vectors decode.

## 1. Decision

1. Sub-64 coded dimensions stay **unsupported** on the AVD backend.
2. The boundary is **not** implemented by padding or cropping. Declaring a padded frame
   size to the decoder is rejected as a design: it changes `MiCols`/`MiRows`, which drive
   partition syntax during decode, so it corrupts the decode rather than merely changing
   the visible crop (§4).
3. The enforced limit today is a **kernel driver guard**, not a demonstrated firmware
   limit (§3.3). Prior notes describing a "kernel minimum 64x64" as a hardware property
   overstate the available evidence.
4. Two bounded children follow (§6): correcting capability reporting, which needs no
   hardware, and a guarded experiment to establish whether the firmware itself accepts a
   sub-64 declared frame size, which needs kernel authorisation and a decoder.

## 2. The affected vectors, classified from parsed bitstreams

`tests/vp9-sub64-scan.py` extracts the first frame of each vector from its container,
parses the VP9 uncompressed header (specification 6.2) and reports the coded frame size,
the render (displayed) size, profile, bit depth, chroma subsampling and the derived
superblock/tile geometry. Dimensions are **parsed, not inferred from filenames**; the
scanner reports zero name-versus-bitstream mismatches across the family.

Run on the pinned `VP9-TEST-VECTORS` suite (§7):

| Result | Count |
|---|---|
| `vp90-2-02-size-*` vectors scanned | 70 |
| coded width or height below 64 (`below_avd_minimum`) | **60** |
| coded width and height at or above 64 (`within_avd_minimum`) | 10 |
| unparsed | 0 |

Cross-checked against the r11 baseline pass sets, the 60 below-minimum vectors are
**exactly** the 60 recorded VP9 failures of this family: no vector below the minimum is
recorded as passing, and no vector at or above the minimum is recorded as failing. The
scanner exits non-zero if that ever stops holding, so the classification cannot silently
drift from the recorded evidence.

Properties shared by all 70 (parsed, not assumed):

* profile 0, 8-bit, 4:2:0 throughout — none of the 60 is a bit-depth or chroma case;
* **render size equals coded size in every vector** (`render_differs` is false for all 70).
  The streams genuinely code an 8x8 … 66x66 picture; none codes a larger frame for display
  at a smaller size. A "decode large, display small" reading of this family is therefore
  wrong;
* every vector is forced to a **single tile column**: `tile_cols_log2` has a legal range
  that is a pure function of `Sb64Cols`, and for these widths the maximum is 0. Tiling is
  not a variable in this group.

The 60 are the full 8x8 grid of widths and heights `{8, 10, 16, 18, 32, 34, 64, 66}` minus
the four combinations where both dimensions are at least 64 (`64x64`, `64x66`, `66x64`,
`66x66`), which pass. That derivation is reproducible from the suite file alone.

The remaining 29 VP9 baseline failures are out of scope here: 27 resize/scalable streams
([#11](https://github.com/iconidentify/omarchy-m1-video/issues/11) and
[libva-v4l2_request#44](https://github.com/iconidentify/libva-v4l2_request/issues/44)) and
two profile-1 streams outside the advertised 4:2:0 profiles.

## 3. Where the limit originates

Verified by reading the pinned kernel sources directly (§7), not from secondary notes.
None of the shipped patches `0001`–`0015` touches `avd-vp9.c`, so this path is stock.

### 3.1 The enforced check

`avd-vp9.c:627-652`, `validate_dec_params()`:

* `frame_width < 64 || frame_height < 64` → `-EINVAL`;
* then `round_up(width, 64)` / `round_up(height, 16)` must equal the negotiated decoded
  format, or `-EINVAL` with `unexpected bitstream resolution`.

The values checked come from `V4L2_CID_STATELESS_VP9_FRAME`, i.e. the **bitstream-declared
frame size**, not the size of any buffer. The call site (`avd-vp9.c:751`) runs while
preparing the run, **before** the job reaches the firmware, so a rejected stream is never
submitted to the decoder.

### 3.2 The allocation is already padded

The negotiated decoded format is `round_up(w, 64) x round_up(h, 16)` and every per-codec
scratch buffer in `avd_vp9_alloc_bufs()` (`avd-vp9.c:654-728`) is sized from that format,
not from the frame size. An 8x8 stream already negotiates a 64x16 decoded format. **Padding
the allocation therefore changes nothing**: the allocation is not what is rejected.

### 3.3 The guard is conservative, not arithmetic

The kernel's own superblock arithmetic handles sub-64 frames without special-casing:
`sb_64_cols = (((frame_width_minus_1 + 8) >> 3) + 7) >> 3` (`avd-vp9.c:470-471`) evaluates
to 1 for every width from 8 to 64 — no underflow, no division by zero, no zero-sized
allocation. Nothing in the surrounding code requires the frame size to be at least 64.

So `validate_dec_params()`'s `< 64` test is a **driver-side guard**. Whether the AVD
firmware would accept a truthfully-declared sub-64 frame is **unknown and untested**. No
evidence in this repository establishes a firmware minimum; the r11 record shows only that
the kernel rejects these streams. Settling it requires §6.2.

### 3.4 An inconsistency worth recording

`avd_enum_framesizes()` (`avd-v4l2.c:511-529`) advertises `min_width = 1`,
`min_height = 1`, `step_width = 1`, `step_height = 1`, while the same format descriptor
carries `min_width = 64`, `step_width = 64`, `min_height = 64`, `step_height = 16`
(`avd-v4l2.c:424-432`) and `avd_try_output_fmt()` applies exactly those constraints through
`v4l2_apply_frmsize_constraints()`. The kernel therefore **advertises a constraint it does
not honour**, and a client that believes `ENUM_FRAMESIZES` will conclude that 8x8 is
supported.

Consequence in this project's userspace: `try_framesize()`
(`libva-v4l2_request/src/context.c:87-114`) validates the requested picture size against
`ENUM_FRAMESIZES` and so **accepts** a sub-64 context; the stream is rejected later, by the
kernel, at decode-parameter validation. `docs/CORPUS.md` in the driver repository describes
`vp90-2-02-size-08x08.webm` as "rejected in userspace", which the source does not support.
Correcting that wording is part of §6.1.

## 4. Why padding or cropping is not admissible

The only way to make one of these streams reach the firmware today is to declare a frame
size of at least 64 while the bitstream codes a smaller one. That is not a presentation
detail; it changes how the bitstream is decoded:

* VP9 derives `MiCols = (FrameWidth + 7) >> 3` and `MiRows` from the declared frame size.
  For an 8-pixel-wide frame `MiCols` is 1; declaring 64 makes it 8.
* Partition decoding is conditioned on that grid: availability of rows and columns at the
  frame edge determines whether a partition symbol is read or an implicit split is used.
  Changing `MiCols` therefore changes the syntax read from the very first superblock, and
  the entropy-coded tile data desynchronises immediately. The result is not a larger
  picture to be cropped; it is a different, wrong decode.
* VP9 reference scaling compounds this. Scale factors are computed from each reference's
  dimensions against the current frame's dimensions, so a frame decoded under a falsified
  size poisons every later frame that references it. The acceptance criterion that a
  padding path must "account for reference scaling and hash the exact visible crop" cannot
  be met, because the pixels inside the crop are already wrong.

No resampling or crop-and-compare step can hide this, and none may be used to make a
checksum match. The padding approach is rejected on these grounds alone, independently of
what the firmware would accept.

The remaining honest option is to declare the **true** sub-64 size and relax the kernel
guard — §6.2 — which is a kernel change requiring authorisation and hardware evidence.

## 5. Capability reporting

The current reporting is wrong in both directions and does not describe the backend:

| Attribute | Reported now | Backend reality (`avd-v4l2.c:424-432`) |
|---|---|---|
| `VASurfaceAttribMinWidth` | 1 | 64 |
| `VASurfaceAttribMinHeight` | 1 | 64 |
| `VASurfaceAttribMaxWidth` | 65536 | 4096 for VP9 and H.264; 16384 for HEVC and AV1 |
| `VASurfaceAttribMaxHeight` | 65536 | 4096 for VP9 and H.264; 16384 for HEVC and AV1 |

`libva-v4l2_request/src/surface.c:266-289` hardcodes these four values instead of deriving
them from the device. A client asking the driver what it supports is told 1x1 to 65536x65536
for every codec on every backend.

Required behaviour, per this ticket's acceptance criteria: capability reporting must expose
the **actual** minimum and maximum for the selected backend, and input below the minimum
must be rejected before decoder submission. Today the first is false and the second holds
only by way of the kernel's own check, because the driver's `ENUM_FRAMESIZES`-based gate is
defeated by §3.4. Both belong to the child in §6.1; this ticket does not change driver
source.

## 6. Implementation children

### 6.1 Report the real dimension limits and reject below them in userspace

Owning layer: `libva-v4l2_request` (driver). No hardware, no kernel change.

* Derive `VASurfaceAttribMin/MaxWidth/Height` from `VIDIOC_ENUM_FRAMESIZES` for the
  selected coded format, with a documented fallback when the ioctl is absent.
* Reject a context below the real minimum at `vaCreateContext`, so a below-minimum stream
  fails without reaching the kernel, and record the existing kernel rejection as the
  backstop rather than the primary gate.
* Because the device currently advertises `min_width = 1` (§3.4), the driver cannot learn
  the true minimum from `ENUM_FRAMESIZES` alone; the child must decide between a
  backend-keyed value and a kernel fix that makes the advertisement match the constraint
  the kernel already applies.
* Correct the `docs/CORPUS.md` "rejected in userspace" wording to name the layer that
  actually rejects.
* Acceptance: offline tests only; the exact r11 pass sets must be unchanged, since no
  currently passing stream is affected.

### 6.2 Establish whether the firmware accepts a truthful sub-64 frame size

Owning layer: kernel patch in this repository. **`needs:hardware` and
`needs:kernel-approval`**; blocked until both are granted.

* Experiment: relax `validate_dec_params()`'s `< 64` test only, keeping the
  `round_up(w, 64) x round_up(h, 16)` format agreement intact, and submit the true frame
  size for a small ordered subset — `vp90-2-02-size-08x08`, `08x64`, `64x08`, `34x34`,
  `66x32` — under the hardware guard, comparing against the software decode.
* Stop conditions: any decoder fault, watchdog or wedge ends the experiment; no
  unload/reload recovery loop; the decoder must be left idle.
* Possible outcomes: the firmware decodes correctly, in which case a scoped kernel patch
  plus exact acceptance vectors becomes a further child; or it faults or produces wrong
  pixels, in which case the 64 minimum is recorded as a **demonstrated** backend limit and
  §1 becomes final with evidence instead of inference.
* Until this runs, no support claim changes and the 60 vectors stay `expected_rejection`.

## 8. Evidence limits

* **No hardware was used.** This session had no Apple Silicon linux-asahi host and no AVD
  decoder, reserved none, and ran no decode. Every statement about the kernel and driver
  comes from reading the pinned sources; every statement about vector contents comes from
  parsing the vectors offline.
* Source inspection does not prove the behaviour of the loaded module binary on any
  particular machine.
* The claim in §3.3 that the guard is conservative is a statement about the **kernel code**,
  not about the firmware. The firmware's actual minimum is untested — that is exactly what
  §6.2 exists to establish, and it must not be reported as a known limit before then.
* The scanner reads only the first frame of each vector. That is sufficient for this family,
  whose streams are single-resolution, but it is not a general per-frame resolution audit.
* `tests/vp9-sub64-scan-test.py` exercises the scanner against synthetic headers and
  containers it builds itself; the real-corpus run above was performed once, offline, and
  is not reproduced in CI, because the vectors may not be redistributed.
